notes: HVS11: included as follow_up because T:p4-b1 refers to its discovery as HVS11 and discusses its angular/velocity relationship to Sextans; the paper does not independently remeasure its present-day escape speed. HE 0437-5439: included as follow_up because T:p4-b2 calls it an HVS, notes its prior discovery, and considers GC versus LMC origins. SDSS J121150.27+143716.2: included as follow_up because T:p6-b5 and T:p6-b6 call it an HVS candidate/binary and consider a nonstandard satellite-debris origin; follow_up applies regardless of the current boundness interpretation, and no component identifiers are supplied for the binary. The collective red-cross sample in Figure 1 (I:p2-b0) is not expanded into individual entries because the caption gives only an open-ended naming convention rather than a complete, unambiguous member list; the synthetic LMC populations are not individual stars.

HVS11: Target HVS11 is mentioned in T:p4-b1 as being within 3.9° of Sextans and having a “260 km s−1 relative velocity ... towards Sextans.” That velocity is relative to Sextans and is not reported as a heliocentric or barycentric line-of-sight radial velocity, so it was not extracted under the radial_velocity definition. No other eligible positional, distance, parallax, proper-motion, velocity, Galactocentric, or bound-probability values for HVS11 are reported.

HE 0437-5439: HE 0437-5439 is mentioned only qualitatively in T:p4-b2: it is the single HVS plotted in Figure 1 lying in the southern celestial hemisphere, discovered by Edelmann et al. (2005), with a flight time longer than the main-sequence lifetime, so either it is a blue straggler ejected from the GC or originated in the LMC. No numerical position, distance, parallax, proper motion, radial velocity, galactocentric radius, rest-frame speed, or bound/unbound probability is reported for this star, so no quantities could be extracted.

SDSS J121150.27+143716.2: The paper is a population-model study of LMC-ejected HVSs. SDSS J121150.27+143716.2 is only discussed briefly (T:p6-b5, T:p6-b6); the sole numerical quantity explicitly tied to this star is its Galactic rest-frame velocity of 571.3 km/s from Németh et al. (2016). No RA, Dec, distance, parallax, proper motion or radial velocity are reported specifically for this star. The 260 km/s relative velocity in T:p4-b1 refers to HVS11, a different object, and is not attributed to the target star.
